text: Long ago, by the river Tamasaa, the sage Vaalmeeki saw a hunter's arrow strike one of two krauncha birds.
sub: Long ago, by the river Tamasa, the sage Valmiki saw a hunter's arrow strike one of two krauncha birds.
asr: Long ago, by the river Tamasa, the sage Valmiki saw a hunter's arrow strike one of two krauncha birds.

text: His grief poured out as a verse... the first poem, it is said. And in that rhythm, he sang the story of Raama, in seven books.
sub: His grief poured out as a verse — the first poem, it is said — and in that rhythm he sang the story of Rama, in seven books.
asr: His grief poured out as a verse — the first poem, it is said — and in that rhythm he sang the story of Rama, in seven books.

text: Prince Raama of Ah-yodhyaa won Princess Seetaa, by breaking the mighty bow of Shiva.
sub: Prince Rama of Ayodhya won Princess Sita by breaking the mighty bow of Shiva.
asr: Prince Rama of Ayodhya won Princess Sita by breaking the mighty bow of Shiva.

text: But on the eve of his crowning, Queen Kaikayee claimed two old promises. Her own son, Bharata, would rule; and Raama would live fourteen years in the forest.
sub: But on the eve of his crowning, Queen Kaikeyi claimed two old promises: her son Bharata would rule, and Rama would live fourteen years in the forest.
asr: But on the eve of his crowning, Queen Kaikeyi claimed two old promises: her son Bharata would rule, and Rama would live fourteen years in the forest.

text: Raama went without anger, with Seetaa, and his brother Lakshmana. Bharata ruled only in his name, with Raama's sandals on the throne.
sub: Rama went without anger, with Sita and his brother Lakshmana. Bharata ruled only in his name, with Rama's sandals on the throne.
asr: Rama went without anger, with Sita and his brother Lakshmana. Bharata ruled only in his name, with Rama's sandals on the throne.

text: In the forest, Raavana, the ten-headed king of Lanka, lured Raama away with a golden deer... and carried Seetaa off, through the sky.
sub: In the forest, Ravana, the ten-headed king of Lanka, lured Rama away with a golden deer — and carried Sita off through the sky.
asr: In the forest, Ravana, the ten-headed king of Lanka, lured Rama away with a golden deer — and carried Sita off through the sky.

text: Searching for her, Raama found allies: the monkey king, Sugreeva, and wise, mighty Hanumaan.
sub: Searching for her, Rama found allies: the monkey king Sugriva, and wise, mighty Hanuman.
asr: Searching for her, Rama found allies: the monkey king Sugriva, and wise, mighty Hanuman.

text: Hanumaan leapt across the ocean, found Seetaa in a grove of ashoka trees, and gave her Raama's ring.
sub: Hanuman leapt across the ocean, found Sita in a grove of ashoka trees, and gave her Rama's ring.
asr: Hanuman leapt across the ocean, found Sita in a grove of ashoka trees, and gave her Rama's ring.

text: An army of monkeys built a bridge of stones to Lanka. Raama defeated Raavana, and came home to be crowned.
sub: An army of monkeys built a bridge of stones to Lanka. Rama defeated Ravana, and came home to be crowned.
asr: An army of monkeys built a bridge of stones to Lanka. Rama defeated Ravana, and came home to be crowned.

text: In the last book, which many scholars believe was added later, Seetaa found refuge with Vaalmeeki, where her twin sons learned his poem, and sang it before Raama himself.
sub: In the last book, which many scholars believe was added later, Sita found refuge with Valmiki, where her twin sons learned his poem, and sang it before Rama himself.
asr: In the last book, which many scholars believe was added later, Sita found refuge with Valmiki, where her twin sons learned his poem, and sang it before Rama himself.

text: Grief by a river became a poem. And people have been singing it, ever since.
sub: Grief by a river became a poem. And people have been singing it ever since.
asr: Grief by a river became a poem. And people have been singing it ever since.
